intro: Campaigns, votes and results: how an election is told in Spanish.
b1.texto:
**Before.** The government **convoca elecciones**: **generales**, **autonómicas** (regional) or **municipales**. The parties choose **un candidato**, write **un programa electoral** and start **la campaña**, with **mítines** and **debates**. **Los sondeos** predict the result. The day before the vote is **la jornada de reflexión**, when campaigning is forbidden.

**The day.** Each **votante** goes to **un colegio electoral**, takes **una papeleta**, puts it in an envelope and drops it in **la urna**. You can also **votar en blanco**, cast **un voto nulo** or **abstenerte**. The percentage of people who vote is **la participación**; the rest is **la abstención**.

**After.** Votes become **escaños**. A party with more than half has **mayoría absoluta**. If nobody has it, the parties **pactan** and form **una coalición**. The others are **la oposición**.

**The chambers.** In Spain, **los diputados** sit in **el Congreso** and **los senadores** in **el Senado**. Together they are **las Cortes**.

**The three powers.** **El poder legislativo**, **el ejecutivo** and **el judicial**.

**Losing power.** A politician **dimite**. A government falls after **una moción de censura**. Power taken by force is **un golpe de Estado**, and what follows is **una dictadura**.

**Verbs with prepositions.** **Votar a** un partido, **presentarse a** las elecciones, **pertenecer a** un partido, **abstenerse de** votar.
b2.f0: At eight in the evening the polling stations closed and one of the longest nights in memory began.
b2.f1: Turnout had been seventy per cent, five points more than the polls were predicting.
b2.f2: With half the ballot papers counted, no party was getting close to an absolute majority.
b2.f3: The government's candidate had lost twenty seats, but was still the one with most votes.
b2.f4: Shortly before midnight, the leader of the opposition announced that she was willing to make a deal with anyone who respected her programme.
b2.f5: Nobody resigned that night, although more than one member of parliament was left without a seat.
b2.f6: Analysts agree that, unless a coalition is formed, new elections will have to be called before the summer.
b4.pregunta: According to the text, did any party win an absolute majority?
b4.o0.refuerzo: Ningún partido se acercaba a la mayoría absoluta.
b4.o2.refuerzo: Its leader offered to make deals.
b5.pregunta: According to the text, what will happen if no coalition is formed?
b5.o1.refuerzo: The text does not say that.
b5.o2.refuerzo: The text does not say that.
b6.pregunta: The box where you put your vote is…
b6.o2.refuerzo: That is a seat in parliament.
b7.pregunta: Complete: I always vote for the same party.
b7.o2.refuerzo: In Spain the usual form is votar a.
b8.pregunta: Complete: unless a coalition is formed…
b8.o0.refuerzo: A menos que takes the subjunctive.
b8.o1.refuerzo: A menos que takes the subjunctive.
b8.o2.refuerzo: A menos que takes the subjunctive.
b9.o1.explicacion: Dimitir is to resign of one's own will.
b10.traduccion: The government has called an election for May.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write an analysis of the last elections in your country: results, surprises and consequences.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Explain aloud why many people do not vote, and whether voting should be compulsory.
